source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Enter BMC-Web -> Overview.
2. Check Power information.
3. Click "View more" to check.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria: All information should match SPEC definition.

deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return FULL pretty-printed JSON from /redfish/v1/Chassis/system/Power (PowerControl/power readings) so user confirms the BMC web "power information" page shows the correct data. No RISK (read-only).

historical_reviews.deepseek: YES identifies one common legacy Redfish power resource but assumes ChassisId `system`, bypasses Overview and `View more`, does not define which readings or tolerances constitute `all information`, and overlooks platforms using PowerSubsystem/Sensors/PowerSupply resources. `-k` plus exposed credentials are unsafe, and `No RISK` ignores adjacent host power/limit controls.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION / CHANGED correctly adds stable operating state, units/tolerances, chassis/sensor identity, freshness and no-power-action controls. This review adds source-selection by advertised links/schema, separates dynamic telemetry from static limits/health, requires capture-window tolerance and disallows automatic re-read until values happen to match.
historical_reviews.round_02: Entry 855/2291 accepts the fixed legacy URI as a direct-run test and does not bind the chassis, preserve the UI workflow, define sensor identities/units/tolerances or separate telemetry observation from dangerous power and limit-setting actions.
historical_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: No sequence-1018 draft exists in the invalidated 1,000-record run.
historical_reviews.v3_1: ED-33 preserves Overview and View-more; ED-34 treats field/tolerance/load-state definitions as Project readiness; ED-35 rejects a single API dump as equivalent to the full UI/SPEC check; ED-38 prohibits power operations or limit changes, requires explicit recovery, no automatic retry and engineer-owned verdict.

original_test_intent: Verify that every Project-required Power information field displayed on the BMC Overview and `View more` belongs to the intended chassis/component, uses the correct units/state semantics and agrees with the approved SPEC or allowed live-telemetry tolerance, without changing power state or power policy.
original_method: Establish a defined stable host/load and PSU topology, capture the Overview power summary, open `View more` once and collect all required fields. Discover the target chassis and vendor-supported read-only power resources from advertised links, map UI values to sensor/power-control/power-supply identities, and compare static properties exactly and dynamic readings within approved time/tolerance bounds.
manual_activity: The Project engineer defines the in-scope power fields, component/sensor mapping, stable system condition and exact-versus-toleranced acceptance rules. Automation can capture and correlate read-only UI/API telemetry, while live variability, platform-specific aggregation and the final verdict remain engineer-owned.
required_inputs: Exact BMC endpoint/certificate, controller firmware/WebUI build, target chassis and host power state
Power-information matrix naming each UI field, source component/sensor, units, static/dynamic nature, expected value or permitted range/tolerance and required health/status
Stable workload/load band, PSU population/feed/redundancy state, sampling window and acceptable UI-to-API timestamp skew
Overview and View-more selectors/routes, account role, locale/format, loading/freshness indicators and display rounding rules
Vendor mapping to advertised Chassis Power, PowerSubsystem, PowerSupply, Sensor, metric or OEM resources with schema/version semantics
Protected authentication, redaction, power-control/limit-setting exclusions and approved recovery if an unintended action occurs
safety_requirements: Do not issue system Reset actions, chassis power actions, PSU/outlet controls, power-cap/limit writes, enable/disable operations, apply buttons or any PATCH/POST/DELETE request.
Do not assume ChassisId `system` or force the legacy `/Power` model. Discover the intended Chassis and follow its advertised power, subsystem, sensor and metric links appropriate to the platform.
Bind every value to a sensor/component and unit. Do not accept zero, null, unavailable, stale or aggregate readings without the Project-defined semantic and health/freshness evidence.

For live watts/current/voltage/energy data, capture UI and API within a bounded interval under the approved stable condition; do not demand string equality between differently averaged or rounded samples.
Do not use `curl -k`, expose credentials or clear dmesg, syslog, SEL, power or audit logs. The page is a high-impact control surface even when the selected operation is read-only.

Navigate/read once and stop without automatic retry on power-state change, task/action creation, control focus/submission, sensor identity mismatch, unstable load, timestamp ambiguity or unexpected reachability loss.
agent_execution_scope: Verify BMC/chassis identity, host power state, PSU/feed topology and stable load band before observing any power values.
Capture Overview and invoke only the read-only `View more` navigation, recording field labels, values, units, status and freshness indicators.

Read the advertised vendor-supported power/sensor resources over trusted access, correlate each sample by identity and timestamp, and apply only engineer-approved rounding, aggregation and tolerances.
Report static mismatches and dynamic deltas/uncertainty separately, preserve logs and proof of no control request, and never issue DUT PASS/FAIL or retry automatically.
engineer_actions: Approve the power field/sensor/component matrix, platform resource mapping, stable condition and static/dynamic acceptance rules.
Approve units, rounding, sampling/averaging windows, tolerances, treatment of unavailable values and strict exclusions for power/limit controls.
Review timestamped UI/API/SPEC comparisons and proof that host power/policy did not change, then issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: A read-only legacy Power GET may be useful if the discovered target chassis advertises it, but the fixed ID and resource cannot be assumed and the payload does not cover the required WebUI path or all modern/vendor fields. It also lacks sample timing, identity, unit and tolerance logic and uses unsafe TLS/credential handling.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Using trusted TLS and protected authentication, discover the target Chassis and its advertised Power/PowerSubsystem/Sensors/metrics or OEM resources, then collect only mapped read-only fields during the approved stable window and correlate them with Overview/View-more timestamps and the signed matrix. Send no writes or actions.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The Overview, `View more`, all-information SPEC criterion, absent Script and 10/0-minute estimates remain preserved; read-only resource queries supplement rather than replace the UI and do not authorize power control.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use schema/link discovery to build a timestamped, component-keyed power dataset; classify fields as static or dynamic; correlate summary/detail UI values with the appropriate sensor/metric sources under one controlled load state; compare by exact rule or approved tolerance.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: The exact chassis, PSU/feed topology, BMC firmware/WebUI build and Redfish/OEM power model selected by the Project.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record Chassis and power-related `@odata.type` values because legacy Power and newer PowerSubsystem/PowerSupply/Sensor models can coexist or differ by implementation.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: DMTF Redfish Power, PowerSubsystem, PowerSupply and Sensor data models, vendor UI/resource mapping and signed Project power-information specification.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Retains the required UI navigation, removes fixed resource assumptions and supplies identity, sampling, units and tolerance rules while keeping all power controls out of scope.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A single read validates neither long-term accuracy nor transient response; UI/API agreement does not calibrate sensors against external instruments; telemetry observation does not test power actions, redundancy transitions or power-cap enforcement.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Target identity, topology/load state, field/source map, units, sampling/tolerances, UI/API schema mapping, credentials, safety and recovery.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Dynamic values can legitimately differ because of latency/averaging; wrong chassis/sensor aggregation can appear plausible; adjacent controls can immediately reset or power off the host.

project_override_considerations: A Project may use newer Redfish resources, a vendor read-only telemetry API or an external meter as corroboration, but must keep Overview/View-more checkpoints, record the actual source/tool and coverage difference, obtain engineer approval and never infer power-control or sensor-calibration PASS from display consistency alone.
expected_evidence: Target BMC/chassis, firmware/WebUI build, trusted certificate, host power state, PSU/feed/redundancy topology and stable load evidence
Signed power field/component/sensor/unit matrix with static expectations or dynamic range/tolerance, sampling and freshness rules
Redacted Overview and View-more screenshots/DOM/routes with field labels, values, units, statuses and capture timestamps
Discovered Chassis and advertised power-related resource/schema evidence plus timestamped mapped API/OEM samples
Per-field UI-summary/UI-detail/API/SPEC comparison showing exact results, dynamic deltas, rounding/averaging window, unavailable/stale values and uncertainty
Proof no power/limit/control/action request occurred and host/BMC state remained unchanged; preserved logs, limitations and engineer-owned verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently define a Power information display/SPEC comparison. The open field matrix and DeepSeek's fixed legacy endpoint are incompleteness and method-fit issues, not contradictory Master purposes.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The read-only UI purpose is clear. Chassis/resource mapping, field selection, stable operating condition and tolerances are normal Project execution inputs, so the row is PACKAGE rather than permanently BLOCKED.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Changes YES to PACKAGE, makes its legacy resource conditional on discovery and adds UI coverage, schema-aware source mapping, sampling/tolerance logic and strict exclusion of power controls.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retains its safe hybrid telemetry approach and strengthens legacy-versus-current resource selection, dynamic/static separation, capture uncertainty and no automatic re-read.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.round_02: Replaces direct-run acceptance of a fixed unbounded payload with a timestamped chassis/sensor-specific UI/API/SPEC comparison.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: No prior invalid draft exists for this sequence.

review_improvement: Prevents a wrong chassis, stale/zero sensor or asynchronous rounded sample from being called correct, and prevents a read-only information check from accidentally exercising host power or power-limit controls.
independent_technical_reasoning: Power pages combine live telemetry, health, static capacity/limits and sometimes direct controls. Live values are time-dependent and may be aggregated or rounded differently across UI and API, whereas static ratings and states use different acceptance rules. Platform Redfish models also vary between legacy Power and newer subsystem/sensor resources. Correct review therefore requires advertised-link discovery, component identity and synchronized tolerance-aware comparison under a defined load, with all control paths excluded.
